scope: Static contract review of the existing named-object root/resource path. No test, converter, native CAD application, or kernel was run in this pass.

primaryReferences.topic: DXF object ownership and group-code ordering
primaryReferences.observation: Autodesk warns that common group-code tables show usual order, not a stable required order; graphical-object material references use hard-pointer code 347.
Code 280 is the hard-owner flag, 281 is duplicate-record cloning policy, and each dictionary entry is a repeated name code 3 plus handle code 350.
The derived AcDbDictionaryWithDefault subclass adds code 340, a hard pointer to the default object; this is a distinct edge from the dictionary's repeated code-350 entries.
LAYOUT embeds an AcDbPlotSettings prefix and separately references its paper-space BLOCK_RECORD (330), last active VIEWPORT (331), optional named/base UCS (345/346), and shade plot (333).
MATERIAL contains many typed color, map, transform, illumination, and procedural fields and is owned by the NOD ACAD_MATERIAL entry.
TABLESTYLE repeats cell-level text, height, alignment, colors, data/unit types, and border state; scalar header retention is not the complete object.
The DXF placeholder record consists of its object identity and common ownership/reactor fields; its significance here is the typed default-pointer target and identity, not a large property body.
A DICTIONARYVAR stores one schema value and a string value under ACDBVARIABLEDICTIONARY; it is not merely an arbitrary untyped dictionary child.

The published DXF table places the AcDbVisualStyle marker before description/type and lists the internal-use flag at code 291; the separate modern 58-property profile still requires producer-witnessed grammar.

localFindings.finding: The nine observed inherited no-op callback families still have no concrete dx_data collection: DictionaryWithDefault, AcDbPlaceholder, MLineStyle, MLeaderStyle, TableStyle, DetailViewStyle, SectionViewStyle, Scale, and DictionaryVar.

DRW_DictionaryWithDefault copy construction/assignment copies the default handle but resets m_dxfDefaultEntrySeen; hasCompleteDxfPayload can therefore become false after the adapter's required owned copy.
The current routed named-DICTIONARY writer emits code 281 and repeated code-3/code-350 entries but does not emit the modeled hardOwner/code-280 flag.
DRW_Material::parseCode decodes only name/description; writeMaterial emits only those fields. The raw-net preserves DXF-origin records, but a DWG-origin material has no raw DXF record to replay.
DRW_TableStyle::parseCode decodes only top-level scalar fields and explicitly leaves row/cell subrecords to the raw-net; the current dxfRW API/source has no writeTableStyle method.

The typed LAYOUT model/writer already covers the documented plot-settings prefix and multiple references, and the writer remaps those references. Its coverage still requires focused graph joins and version-specific checks before admission.

SCALE/DICTIONARYVAR/MLINESTYLE/MLEADERSTYLE writers exist. MLINESTYLE's public element model contains RGB and newer linetype-handle fields not emitted by the current code. MLEADERSTYLE's 340-343 references are currently written from stored values directly, so handle-remap behavior must be checked before graph closure.
No typed DXF writer is declared for DICTIONARYWDFLT, ACDBPLACEHOLDER, TABLESTYLE, DETAILVIEWSTYLE, or SECTIONVIEWSTYLE.

planChanges: Keep f.4a as owned callback storage, and preserve DICTIONARYWDFLT's source-completeness evidence across copies; do not add interface pure virtuals.
Make one source-field to model-field to output-tag to graph-edge matrix the first f.4b deliverable; do not start the composed CLI gate from callback counts.
Prioritize families with existing writers only after mapping their full stored fields and handle remaps; SCALE/DICTIONARYVAR are the shortest candidates.

Treat MATERIAL, TABLESTYLE, DICTIONARYWDFLT/default PLACEHOLDER, DETAILVIEWSTYLE, and SECTIONVIEWSTYLE as explicit full-root blockers until their payload and writers are complete or the conversion refuses before publication.
Include DICTIONARY code-280 ownership policy, default code-340 hard-pointer role, LAYOUT's separate 330/331/333/345/346 edges, and entity-to-MATERIAL code-347 edges in graph closure.
Add reordered DXF group-code controls because published Autodesk tables describe usual order rather than a parser-required sequence.
